pull.title: wallet: Add deriveHDKey interface
pull.body:
This PR adds a wallet interface for derivehdkey.

The motivation is the same as #35436 and #34861. The derivehdkey RPC exists
(#32784), but the GUI does not go through RPC, so the logic is currently out of
its reach. A dedicated wallet interface makes it available for multisig setup.
Alongside the addhdkey interface, this lets the GUI add an HD key and derive a
shareable xpub from it. Tracked as the deriveHDKey item in #35645.

Key changes:
- Move the key selection and derivation logic from the RPC into CWallet::DeriveHDKey, including the wallet and argument checks.
- Have the RPC call CWallet::DeriveHDKey and translate its WalletError using HandleWalletErrorCode.
- Add interfaces::Wallet::deriveHDKey, which returns the derived xpub and key origin. Private materials are not exposed through the interface.
- Add interface tests for derivation and error forwarding. Update the functional tests for the changed error codes and unlock message.

rpc: Move derivehdkey checks into helper

Move the watch-only, hardened-path, unlock and xpub-validity checks into
DeriveHDKey in their existing order, retaining the v32 RPC codes and
messages. The RPC still decodes its inputs and holds the wallet lock.

Input parsing now precedes the watch-only check, so a malformed path
supplied to a watch-only wallet reports the path error first.

All this is duplicated from RPC code. Why not just make both the interface and the RPC rely on the same code? Because of both using different code functions, they both return different error codes for same errors.

Also probably this commit could be split in different commits. First a preparatory commit that creates the DeriveHDKey function + testing, then a commit rebasing the RPC to use it, then a commit creating the interface. You can check #34861 for a commit structure idea :)
Right, removed this branch
Squashed, SelectHDKey returns util::Expected from the start now.

Done. Split into "Add CWallet::DeriveHDKey" and "Add deriveHDKey interface".

On sharing code with the RPC: it already calls SelectHDKey(). What's left is the watch-only, hardened-path and unlock guards, which pin the error codes wallet_derivehdkey.py asserts (-4, -8, -13).

DeriveHDKey() returns GenericError for every failure, so routing the rest through it would turn "Unable to derive HD key at the requested path" from -8 into -5. Keeping -8 would need a new WalletErrorCode just so one caller can pick a different number, which src/wallet/types.h:48-50 warns against.
Fixed
Now both the interface and the RPC rely on the same CWallet::DeriveHDKey

Haven't reviewed yet, but re changing error codes:
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35690#issuecomment-4939490752

I don't think the current structure is what Ram meant.
First commit duplicates code now, and the 2ndo removes it which is confusing. Let me suggest another approach:

A way to do this in a clean and easily readable way is to first extract the RPC functionality into some helper function inside the `rpc/wallet.cpp`, then have another move-only commit that moves that helper function into `wallet.cpp`. And then another one changing the error codes.

So tldr;

1. Extract in the same rpc file the functionality of `DeriveHDKey` into a `DeriveHDKey` helper function
2. Change the error codes.
3. Move the `DeriveHDKey` function to `wallet.cpp`.
4. Add the interface

This is easy to review because the extracting code is in the same file and does not change much. Both old code and the new function are in the same commit.
The change errors is pretty straight forward.
The move commit can easily be reviewed with --color-moved=dimmed-zebra

Left a proposal here:
https://github.com/polespinasa/bitcoin/commits/pr-36070/

comments.body: At this point we should add an invalid parameter error code to at least distinguish caller problems from wallet problems. I'm fine with collapsing `INVALID_ADDRESS_OR_KEY` with `INVALID_PARAMETER`, but collapsing those into `WALLET_ERROR` makes the error code to the user too vague. `WALLET_ERROR` is really for "something bad happened in the wallet internally", as opposed to "the user gave us a bad argument".
